heading: What satellite-linked tags do
body_md: Tags record locations when animals surface or pass receivers (depending on tag type). **This demo uses synthetic pings only.** Real tags combine sensors and transmit bursts opportunistically—not continuously.

heading: Why pings are not continuous
body_md: Transmission depends on battery life, antenna orientation, surfacing behavior, and ocean conditions. **Gaps are normal** and should be framed honestly to the public.

heading: Why some locations may be uncertain
body_md: Each ping carries implied uncertainty depending on sensor mode and environmental noise. Demo uses `location_quality` labels (**high/medium/low**) as a teaching placeholder—not operational Argos codes.

heading: Why shark movement matters
body_md: Understanding routes informs habitat protections, avoids misleading single-point narratives, and connects fisheries-independent observations with broader ecosystem questions.

heading: How anglers contribute
body_md: Responsible reporting, tagging collaborations, and ethical handling amplify conservation outcomes when paired with transparent science communication.

heading: Responsible handling and release
body_md: Follow regional guidance for shark-safe handling and rapid release (for example NOAA Fisheries shark-handling summaries and state fishery bulletins). **Never approach wildlife recklessly for photographs.**
